simple.meaning: אֵיד (ʼêyd) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “oppression ; by implication misfortune , ruin.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 24 times across Deuteronomy, 2 Samuel, Job, Psalms, Proverbs, and 3 more, beginning at Deuteronomy 32:35. Its meaning is built by comparing the passages where Scripture uses it.

definitions.full: H343. ed אֵיד noun masculine Job 18:12 distress, calamity (under which one bends, compare Arabic burdening ) Bev Jphil. xxvi. 302 derives from Arabic be strong [also oppress, burden ], whence (or ) calamity. — ׳א 21:30 +; construct id. 31:23 +; אֵידי 2Sam 22:19 = Psa 18:19 etc.; — distress, calamity (in poetry chiefly Wisdom Literature & late); Prov 17:5 ; 27:10 . 1 national calam . of Israel (apostate) Jer 18:17 ; Ezek 35:5 ; Obadiah 13 (3 t. in verse); of Egypt Jer 46:21 ; Moab 48:16 ; Edom ( ׳א עֵשָׂו ) 49:8 ; Hazor 49:32 . 2 of righteous sufferer 2Sam 22:19 = Psa 18:19 compare ׳א אֵל i.e. from God Job 31:23 & אֵידָם אָרְחוֺת 30:12 their calamitous paths (suffix reference to bereavement, pain, etc.) 3 often of wicked Job 18:12 ; 21:17 ; 31:3 ; Prov 1:26-27 , (wisd. mocks at; || מַּחַד ) 6:15 ; 24:22 ; also א ׳יוֺם Deut 32:35 ; Job 21:30 (compare above 2Sam 22:19 = Psa 18:19 ; Prov 27:10 ; Jer 18:17 ; 46:21 ; Obadiah 13 (3 t. in verse) where || צָרה יוֺם אֹבֶד יוֺם 46:12 ; 46:14 , compare יהוה יוֺם 46:15 ).
definitions.rootNote: from the same as 181 (in the sense of bending down);

occurrences.englishText: Vengeance is mine, and recompense,
They came on me in the day of my calamity,
His strength will be famished.
“How often is it that the lamp of the wicked is put out,
that the evil man is reserved to the day of calamity,
On my right hand rise the rabble.
Is it not calamity to the unrighteous,
For calamity from God is a terror to me.
He brought me out also into a large place.
I also will laugh at your disaster.
when calamity overtakes you like a storm,
Therefore his calamity will come suddenly.
Whoever mocks the poor reproaches his Maker.
for their calamity will rise suddenly.
Don’t forsake your friend and your father’s friend.
I will scatter them as with an east wind before the enemy.
Also her hired men in the middle of her are like calves of the stall;
“The calamity of Moab is near to come,
Flee! Turn back!
Their camels will be a booty,
“ ‘ “Because you have had a perpetual hostility, and have given over the children of Israel to the power of the sword in the time of their calamity, in the time of the iniquity of the end;
Don’t enter into the gate of my people in the day of their calamity. Don’t look down on their affliction in the day of their calamity, neither seize their wealth on the day of their calamity.
